lines.text: Master's Thesis: Input
AI Collaboration Documentation
Tim Ballaschke
Hochschule für bildende Künste Hamburg
Working version -- 5 October 2026
Editorial note
This document records the visible communication used in the production of the
Master's thesis Input. It contains user prompts, visible assistant responses and
visible progress updates. Hidden system instructions, internal reasoning and tool
telemetry are excluded because they are not part of the human-AI communication.
CGPT-01 to CGPT-04 are earlier ChatGPT materials supplied by the student. FDBK-01
to FDBK-04 are externally supplied review feedback whose authorship was not
independently verified. CDX-01 to CDX-04 are the Codex tasks used to organize
research and production. Exact machine-readable message records, preserved
attachments and SHA-256 manifests are retained with the project. Generated archive
files are regenerated rather than manually edited. DRAFT-01 and DRAFT-02 preserve
two Interaction chapter texts supplied for review; they are not transcriptions of
the later, separately retained Pages manuscript checkpoint. DRAFT-03 preserves the
Operation 1 text supplied to identify overlap with the proposed Operation 2
outline; it is not a source-checked manuscript approval. DRAFT-04 preserves the
subsequent Operation 2 text supplied for stronger critical analysis of commercial
interests and provider power, not an approved revision. DRAFT-05 preserves the
subsequent Operation 2 text supplied for removal of premature SEO discussion. The
chat revision is a proposal, not a new manuscript or full source-verification
checkpoint. DRAFT-06 preserves the Operation 3 text supplied to review coverage of
data routes, storage and additional uses; no revised prose is implied. DRAFT-07
preserves the physical-input section and supplied annotations 02-05 whose targeted
incorporation the student requested. The marked revision remains a proposal, not
an adopted manuscript checkpoint.
CGPT-05 to CGPT-14 are public shared-chat snapshots supplied by the student and
imported on 17 September 2026. They contain 407 user and visible assistant
messages, including 23 visible progress messages. The exact message text is
retained in JSONL; the printed representation adds line wrapping and readable
labels for native citation controls, writing blocks and unsupported symbols.
Hidden reasoning, system/developer context, model memory and tool payloads are
excluded. These snapshots do not certify all branches of the original chats.
Thirteen uploaded files and one linked Word artifact were not retrieved; their
names and message associations are recorded in the project import index and
archive manifests. Provider timestamps distinguish original messages from the
later creation of share links. No token counts or active work durations are
inferred for these external chats.
CGPT-15 and CGPT-16 are two further public shared-chat snapshots supplied by the
student and imported on 18 September 2026. They add 76 messages (38 user prompts
and 38 visible assistant answers). CGPT-15 covers the stepwise drafting of
Surface; CGPT-16 covers the introduction and conclusion. No missing uploads or
linked artifacts are indicated in these two snapshots. The same extraction and
evidence limits apply. The synchronized CDX-03 record also includes the preceding
outlines, wording revisions and the separately authorized Git publication. This
documentation update itself does not publish new files or change the manuscript.
Page references for that edition are recorded in the dated 18 September project
index.
CGPT-17 to CGPT-19 are three further public shared-chat snapshots supplied by the
student and imported on 5 October 2026. They add 220 messages (110 user prompts
and 110 visible assistant answers). CGPT-17 covers a short Surface revision;
CGPT-18 covers a condensed conclusion; CGPT-19 covers stepwise wording and
argument revisions across the introduction, Surface, Interaction, Operation and
conclusion. No missing uploads or linked artifacts are indicated in these three
snapshots. Reused passages are retained and cross-referenced in the dated import
index. A requested or selected wording in a chat is not proof of its inclusion in
the manuscript. CDX-04 records the current documentation import. Current page
references are recorded in the dated 5 October project index; earlier page maps
remain historical editions.
Repeated or reused passages remain in their original conversational context.
Cross-references in the import index prevent treating them as independent
contributions. Import is not evidence that a suggestion was adopted in the
manuscript, nor does it verify scholarly claims made in the conversation. The
hypothetical Steyerl-informed discussion in CGPT-13 is an AI interpretation, not
testimony or confirmed statements by Hito Steyerl. The resumed CDX-03 archive also
includes the previously deferred correction exchanges and the subsequent Surface
planning discussion. Prior dated closure notes retain their historical page
references; citations must be checked against this edition.
Every archive has its own line-number sequence. Thesis citations must therefore
name the archive ID as well as the page and line range. The companion usage
register records where and how an AI contribution was used.
